stories.headline: 3 killed, 2 injured when SUV rolls on Weld County road north of Greeley
stories.summary:
Three young men died and two others were injured Saturday evening after a speeding SUV crashed on Weld County Road 80 near Ault, roughly 12 miles north of Greeley, according to the Colorado State Patrol. The five occupants were all ejected when the 2005 Chevrolet Tahoe veered into a ditch, lost control and rolled as it swerved back onto the road at approximately 5:18 p.m.

The three killed were a 19-year-old from Eaton, a 20-year-old from Eaton and a 19-year-old from Greeley. Their identities will be released by the Weld County Coroner's Office. The driver, a 20-year-old Wyoming man, was airlifted to a hospital in critical condition, while a fourth passenger from Eaton was taken to the hospital with minor injuries.

Eastbound Weld County Road 80 was closed for approximately six hours following the crash before reopening around 11:15 p.m. State patrol officials cited speed as a contributing factor. The crash is under investigation.

stories.headline: Metro Denver drought deepens: Reservoir levels down 20%, cities weigh stricter water restrictions
stories.summary:
Water levels across metro Denver reservoirs are running significantly below seasonal norms, with Highlands Ranch's four reservoirs sitting 20% below where they typically stand in late July, and the broader state reservoir system at 65% to 75% of expected capacity. The conditions stem from Colorado's lowest recorded snowpack since 1941, compounding what state engineer Jason Ullmann called a likely "record drought year."

Cities are responding with escalating enforcement. Aurora has issued nearly 200 fines this summer for water restriction violations, compared with roughly half a dozen last year. Castle Rock last week mandated a two-day-per-week watering limit after voluntary reductions proved insufficient. Denver Water and most other utilities remain at Stage 1 restrictions.

The drought's impact is visible across the region. Clear Creek in Golden is running at just over a quarter of its normal late-July flow — the lowest level since 2002, according to Golden officials. With temperatures expected to remain in the 90s well into the week, water managers say the situation could worsen significantly if winter snowpack again falls short.

stories.headline: Denver DSA eyes November special election to hold at-large City Council seat vacated by Parady
stories.summary:
The Denver chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America is mobilizing to defend an at-large Denver City Council seat that will be vacated when Councilwoman Sarah Parady resigns in August due to health problems. The special election, set for November, will use a plurality-wins format, meaning a candidate can win without a majority — a dynamic that could attract a crowded field.

The November outcome will be temporary: the same seat will appear on the April municipal ballot, where a candidate must win more than 50% of the vote or face a runoff. The DSA is hoping momentum from democratic socialist Melat Kiros's primary upset over longtime Rep. Diana DeGette in Colorado's 1st Congressional District will carry over to the council race.

Parady intends to formally resign on Aug. 5, at which point candidates will have a short window to file. Seven people have already filed for the April election for the same seat. The unusual dual-election structure and the DSA's recent electoral success are expected to generate significant interest across the ideological spectrum.

stories.headline: Colorado schools face new year with slashed mental health funding and new cellphone restrictions
stories.summary:
Colorado school districts are entering the 2026-27 school year confronting the loss of federal mental health grants that paid for therapists, psychologists and individualized student support. The U.S. Department of Education terminated the program in April 2025, citing what it called race-based use of funds — a claim the Colorado Attorney General's Office is challenging in federal court, though districts are budgeting as if the funding will not return.

The funding loss coincides with a new statewide mandate requiring districts to implement cellphone restriction policies. Some schools that have already banned devices report increased student interaction and fewer behavioral disruptions, though administrators say managing both changes simultaneously feels more like a reckoning than a routine transition.

Colorado already ranks below the national average in per-pupil spending, leaving districts heavily reliant on federal programs to fill gaps. Colorado Education Association president Kevin Vick said most districts are planning without the federal mental health dollars, complicating staffing decisions made over the summer ahead of the school year.

stories.headline: Nuggets decline Jalen Pickett's team option; Rockies make seven players available ahead of trade deadline
stories.summary:
The Denver Nuggets have chosen to decline the team option on guard Jalen Pickett ahead of Monday's NBA contract option deadline, according to The Denver Post. The move comes as the Nuggets navigate significant salary cap pressures following the Spencer Jones offer sheet situation with Oklahoma City.

On the baseball side, USA Today MLB insider Bob Nightengale reports that the Colorado Rockies will be active sellers ahead of the August 3 trade deadline, with seven players available. The Rockies, sitting at 42-64 on the season, lost to the Milwaukee Brewers 8-5 on Saturday after winning Friday's game 5-2 behind Tomoyuki Sugano's 10th win.

The Rockies' trade deadline activity will be closely watched as the struggling franchise looks to reshape its roster. Meanwhile, the Nuggets face continued offseason roster decisions as they assess their salary structure around franchise cornerstone Nikola Jokic.

stories.headline: Broncos designate two players to injury lists ahead of training camp; Bonitto launches food bank partnership
stories.summary:
The Denver Broncos placed two players on injury lists ahead of the opening of training camp, though the team said the position battles those players were involved in will continue as scheduled. The designations were announced as the team prepares for its first full camp under new offensive coordinator Davis Webb.

Outside linebacker Nik Bonitto, coming off a strong postseason performance against Buffalo, announced a new food bank partnership as camp opens. Bonitto said his playoff experience gave him confidence heading into the new season, and he is targeting an improved regular-season impact to match his postseason play.

Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph noted the team expects young players to step up in key roles this season. Inside linebacker Red Murdock, this year's Mr. Irrelevant from the NFL Draft, has been described internally as a "tackling machine" and is among the young players drawing attention in camp.

stories.headline: Colorado Buffaloes QB Julian Lewis named a breakout candidate; Buffaloes head to Colorado Springs for fall camp
stories.summary:
Colorado Buffaloes quarterback Julian Lewis has been tabbed as a breakout candidate for the upcoming college football season by The Athletic. Lewis is among several young players drawing attention as the Buffaloes prepare for fall camp, which will be held in Colorado Springs.

Wide receiver DeAndre Moore responded publicly to comments made by Washington Huskies head coach Steve Sarkisian regarding roster personnel, adding a note of intrigue heading into fall camp. Colorado also ranks among the oldest rosters in college football by average age, according to recent analyses.

The Buffaloes' fall camp in Colorado Springs marks a change of scenery as the program builds on its recent national profile under head coach Deion Sanders.

stories.headline: Hiker rescued from Waterton Canyon after heat exhaustion during record-breaking temperatures
stories.summary:
A hiker required rescue Saturday from Waterton Canyon, located southwest of Littleton, after suffering heat exhaustion approximately two miles from the trailhead. The hiker was alone and unable to return to the parking area independently, prompting a 911 call.

West Metro Fire crews responded, located the hiker and transported them back to their vehicle. No hospitalization was reported. The incident occurred during a weekend of record-breaking heat across the Denver metro area, with temperatures climbing above 100 degrees.

West Metro Fire used the rescue as a public safety reminder, urging hikers to check forecasts before heading out, carry ample water, wear sunscreen and recognize early symptoms of heat illness. Crews warned that turning back early is always preferable to requiring an emergency rescue.

stories.headline: Denver man arrested after crash kills passenger in his vehicle
stories.summary:
A 32-year-old man was arrested by Denver Police following a crash that killed a passenger in his vehicle, according to 9News. Details on the location and exact circumstances of the crash were not immediately available, and Denver Police are continuing to investigate.

The arrest adds to a string of serious traffic incidents in the Denver metro area during a summer marked by extreme heat and elevated road activity. Denver Police have not yet released the name of the suspect or the identity of the victim pending next-of-kin notification.

The case is expected to result in felony charges related to the death of the passenger. Further details are anticipated as the investigation proceeds.

stories.headline: Colorado Sun columnist examines Gov. Polis's fractured relationship with state Democrats as term nears end
stories.summary:
Colorado Sun columnist Mario Nicolais examines the political legacy of Gov. Jared Polis, arguing that the two-term Democratic governor will leave office deeply at odds with much of his own party. Nicolais traces Polis's trajectory from a pivotal figure in turning Colorado from a red to a blue state — alongside donors Tim Gill, Pat Stryker and Rutt Bridges — to a lame-duck executive many Democrats would prefer to see exit immediately.

The column notes Polis's early political career, including a costly 2000 State Board of Education race he won by 90 votes and his decade in Congress before running for governor in 2018. Nicolais argues that Polis's recent policy directions have placed him at war with the Democratic establishment that once supported his rise.

With Attorney General Phil Weiser widely viewed as the favorite to succeed Polis, the column frames the governor's final months in office as a study in how quickly political capital can erode. The piece also references speculation about Polis's post-gubernatorial media ambitions.

stories.headline: Parker woman's search for 1896 diary's owner leads her to forgotten founder of DU's law school
stories.summary:
Parker resident Kendall Desmond spent several years piecing together the identity of the author of an 1896 diary that came to her family through a box of old books, ultimately tracing it to George C. Manly — a founder and dean of the University of Denver College of Law and a Republican state senator. Desmond used newspaper archives, DU historical records and genealogical research to confirm the diary's authorship.

Key clues included references to faculty meetings, a "law school," and medical appointments for a woman named Calista, who turned out to be the widow of Manly's brother. Cross-referencing diary entries with newspaper clippings from the 1890s confirmed the match.

Desmond, who describes herself as a history enthusiast and works a corporate job while raising a young child, said the discovery underscored how quickly significant local figures can fade from public memory. Her husband, himself a DU law school graduate, found the connection particularly meaningful.

stories.headline: Denver Gazette columnist reflects on Melat Kiros's primary win and what it signals for Denver's political future
stories.summary:
Denver Gazette contributor Pius Kamau offers a personal reflection on democratic socialist Melat Kiros's primary defeat of longtime U.S. Rep. Diana DeGette in Colorado's 1st Congressional District, arguing the upset reflects a generational shift in Denver's political landscape. Kamau describes DeGette as having become a comfortable fixture rather than an active legislator, and credits Kiros's emergence partly to her dismissal from a law firm after she wrote about Palestinian rights.

Kamau expresses cautious optimism about Kiros's potential in Congress while tempering expectations, noting she will be one of 435 voices in the House. He pushes back against characterizations of democratic socialists as pursuing a communist agenda, framing Kiros's victory as an expression of democratic renewal rather than radical disruption.

The column adds to ongoing local commentary about the significance of Kiros's win for Denver politics and the DSA's growing influence in the city's electoral landscape, following her favored position heading into the November general election.

topStory.headline: Three Killed, Four Wounded in Shooting at Seattle Food Festival Near Space Needle
topStory.summary:
A shooting at the annual Bite of Seattle food festival left three people dead and four others wounded Sunday evening when two suspects opened fire on each other in the crowded Seattle Center, authorities said. The incident began around 6 p.m. local time as thousands of families were attending the outdoor festival, which is held near the city's iconic Space Needle and Climate Pledge Arena. Witnesses described initially mistaking the gunshots for fireworks before fleeing in panic, with some taking shelter inside the Space Needle itself.

Seattle Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said at a late-night press conference that officers already working in the area rushed in and confronted one of the shooters, an action he credited with preventing additional casualties. Two guns were recovered at the scene. One suspect was taken into custody, while a second fled and remained at large as of Monday, with a search ongoing.

Of the seven people struck by gunfire, two were pronounced dead at the scene after CPR failed, and a 56-year-old woman later died at Harborview Medical Center. The four survivors — including a 2-year-old boy, a 39-year-old woman, and a 23-year-old man, all treated at Harborview — were listed in stable condition. A 40-year-old woman with minor injuries declined initial treatment but later sought care at the University of Washington Medical Center.

The federal Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives deployed several agents to the scene, though Seattle police are leading the investigation. Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson said the state SWAT team also responded at Seattle police's request. Seattle Mayor Katie Wilson called the shooting an "unbelievable tragedy and a horrific act of violence" and said more must be done to address gun violence in the city and nationwide.

The Seattle Center draws large crowds year-round as a major tourist and events hub, and the Bite of Seattle festival is one of the region's most attended summer gatherings. Authorities have not released the identities of the victims or the detained suspect. The search for the second suspect continued Monday, and no additional details about a possible motive had been released.
